# Managing principals

Users and groups in Boundary are collectively known as principals. You assign [grants](/boundary/docs/rbac#grant-strings) on [roles](/boundary/docs/domain-model/roles) to principal IDs — the unique IDs of users, groups, or both.

[Users](/boundary/docs/domain-model/users) represent an _internal_ notion of a particular identity, such as a person or a machine. A user can be linked to one or more [account](/boundary/docs/domain-model/accounts) resources through [auth methods](/boundary/docs/domain-model/auth-methods). Accounts represent an _external_ notion of an identity, which lets you switch a user to a new auth method or identity provider without losing their role assignments.

This page describes how to link a user to an existing account, and then authenticate as that user. If you do not already have an auth method and account, refer to [Configure authentication](/boundary/docs/authentication) to create one before you continue. The examples on this page use a password account, but linking a user to an account works the same way regardless of auth method type.

<Note>

All auth methods automatically create ("auto-vivify") a user the first time someone authenticates successfully against an account, if no user is already linked to that account. Manually creating and linking a user, as described in this topic, is useful when you want explicit control over user creation, such as when Terraform manages your Boundary resources. Refer to [What is a primary auth method?](/boundary/docs/authentication#what-is-a-primary-auth-method) for more information.

</Note>

## Create a user

Create a user in the same scope as the account you want to link it to, and then link the two together.

<Tabs>
<Tab heading="CLI" group="cli">

First, create the user resource:

```shell-session
$ boundary users create -name "myuser" -description "My user resource" -scope-id $SCOPE_ID
```

Then link the user to an existing account:

```shell-session
$ boundary users set-accounts -id $USER_ID -account $ACCOUNT_ID
```

</Tab>
<Tab heading="UI" group="ui">

1. Navigate to a scope, then select **Users**.
1. Select **New**.
1. Complete the **Name** and **Description** fields, and select **Save**.
1. From the user's **Accounts** tab, select **Manage**, then select **Add Accounts**.
1. Select the account you want to link, and select **Add Accounts**.

</Tab>
<Tab heading="Terraform" group="terraform">

```hcl
resource "boundary_user" "myuser" {
  name        = "myuser"
  description = "My user resource"

  # Reference the account resource you created for this user
  account_ids = [boundary_account.myuser.id]
  scope_id    = "SCOPE_ID"
}
```

</Tab>
</Tabs>

## Log in

Authenticate as the linked user to confirm the account and user are connected correctly. Use the `authenticate` subcommand for your auth method type. Refer to [Configure authentication](/boundary/docs/authentication) for OIDC, LDAP, and password examples.

```shell-session
$ boundary authenticate password -auth-method-id $PASSWORD_AUTH_METHOD_ID -login-name myuser
```

- To learn more about creating or managing accounts, refer to the CLI [`accounts`](/boundary/docs/commands/accounts) topic or the API [Account service](/boundary/api-docs/account-service) topic.
